notes: 💸 The friction line on Today's picks is now per-share. Until now it assumed the cost of getting out was one ASX tick — the minimum possible. A study today across 1,946 ordinary shares (~94 trading days of daily highs and lows each) found that below 50c that assumption was already right: the exchange's minimum tick IS the dominant cost there, dwarfing the real spread. But above $1 the true spread exceeds one tick on 84–95% of shares — the old line was 2–9× too kind on dearer shares. So each pick card now estimates THIS share's own spread from ~100 days of its stored highs and lows and charges whichever is larger: one tick, or the share's real estimated spread. The label says which one is binding, the tooltip publishes the study — including the half that says the old assumption was fine where the bot lives — and the 'edge clears 2× friction' verdict now uses the honest number. Display only; the bot's decisions are unchanged until Monday's baseline.
